import io
import re
import hashlib
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
import extract_msg
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

# 1. Retrieve the file buffer directly from N8N's binary memory
binary_item = _input.binary['submitted_file']
file_bytes = binary_item.get_bytes()
file_name = binary_item.file_name.lower()

# Security: File size check (5MB)
if len(file_bytes) > 5 * 1024 * 1024:
    raise ValueError("File size exceeds 5MB security limit")

# Security: Calculate SHA-256 hash for audit trail (of the email itself)
sha256_hash = hashlib.sha256(file_bytes).hexdigest()

# Hyperlink extraction: catch <a href>, bare http(s) links, and defanged variants
URL_RE = re.compile(r'https?://[^\s"\'<>)\]\}]+', re.IGNORECASE)

def extract_urls(text):
    if not text:
        return []
    found = set()
    for m in URL_RE.finditer(text):
        # strip trailing punctuation that is almost never part of the URL
        u = m.group(0).rstrip('.,;:!?)\']}>"')
        found.add(u)
    return sorted(found)

def sanitize_html(html):
    soup = BeautifulSoup(html, 'html.parser')
    for tag in ['script', 'iframe', 'object', 'embed']:
        for element in soup.find_all(tag):
            element.decompose()
    return soup.get_text(separator='\n', strip=True)

def links_from_html(html):
    """Pull both href attributes AND text URLs from HTML bodies."""
    urls = set()
    if not html:
        return urls
    try:
        soup = BeautifulSoup(html, 'html.parser')
        for a in soup.find_all('a', href=True):
            href = a['href'].strip()
            if re.match(r'^https?://', href, re.IGNORECASE):
                urls.add(href.split('#')[0])
        # also any URL appearing in the raw HTML (img src, style url(), etc.)
        for u in extract_urls(html):
            urls.add(u)
    except Exception:
        pass
    return urls

# 2. Process based on byte streams instead of local files
result = {}

if file_name.endswith('.msg'):
    msg = extract_msg.Message(file_bytes)

    body_html = getattr(msg, 'htmlBody', None) or ''
    body_text = msg.body or ''
    all_urls = set(links_from_html(body_html)) | set(extract_urls(body_text))

    safe_attachments = []
    for att in msg.attachments:
        fn = att.longFilename or att.shortFilename or 'unnamed'
        raw = att.data or b''
        att_sha = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() if raw else None
        safe_attachments.append({
            'filename': re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]', '', fn),
            'content_type': att.mimetype,
            'size': len(raw),
            'sha256': att_sha,
            'ext': ('.' + fn.rsplit('.', 1)[-1].lower()) if '.' in fn else '',
            # first 500 chars of text content only (never executed); non-text = null
            'content_preview': (str(raw[:500]) if att_sha and att.mimetype.startswith('text') else None),
        })
        # attachments can carry their own URLs (e.g. html attachments)
        if att.mimetype and 'html' in att.mimetype:
            all_urls |= links_from_html(raw.decode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    result = {
        'headers': {'From': msg.sender, 'To': msg.to, 'Subject': msg.subject, 'Date': msg.date,
                    'Cc': getattr(msg, 'cc', None), 'ReplyTo': getattr(msg, 'reply_to', None)},
        'body': sanitize_html(body_html) if body_html else sanitize_html(body_text),
        'attachments': safe_attachments,
        'urls': sorted(all_urls),
        'metadata': {'sender': msg.sender, 'subject': msg.subject, 'date': msg.date,
                     'sha256': sha256_hash, 'format': 'msg', 'attachment_count': len(safe_attachments)},
    }
else:
    parsed_email = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(file_bytes)

    body_part = parsed_email.get_body(preferencelist=('html', 'plain'))
    body_content = body_part.get_content() if body_part else ""
    content_type = body_part.get_content_type() if body_part else "text/plain"
    all_urls = links_from_html(body_content) if 'html' in content_type else extract_urls(body_content)

    safe_attachments = []
    for part in parsed_email.iter_attachments():
        fn = part.get_filename() or 'unnamed'
        raw = part.get_payload(decode=True) or b''
        att_sha = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() if raw else None
        ctype = part.get_content_type()
        safe_attachments.append({
            'filename': re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]', '', fn),
            'content_type': ctype,
            'size': len(raw),
            'sha256': att_sha,
            'ext': ('.' + fn.rsplit('.', 1)[-1].lower()) if '.' in fn else '',
            'content_preview': (str(raw[:500]) if att_sha and ctype.startswith('text') else None),
        })
        if 'html' in ctype:
            all_urls |= links_from_html(raw.decode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    result = {
        'headers': dict(parsed_email),
        'body': sanitize_html(body_content) if 'html' in content_type else sanitize_html(body_content),
        'attachments': safe_attachments,
        'urls': sorted(all_urls),
        'metadata': {'sender': parsed_email['From'], 'subject': parsed_email['Subject'],
                     'date': parsed_email['Date'], 'sha256': sha256_hash, 'format': 'eml',
                     'attachment_count': len(safe_attachments)},
    }

# Return structured JSON back to the N8N workflow (feeds the MCP Client investigation)
return result

parameters.content:
## Phishing Email Analysis

Automatically investigate a suspected phishing email and get a plain-language verdict in Telegram. Submit a flagged `.eml` / `.msg` (via a linked Google Sheet / Form) and the workflow parses it, checks the mail authentication, scans every link and attachment, and reports the result.

### How it works
1. A new sheet row supplies a Google Drive link to the email; it is downloaded and validated.
2. A Python node extracts headers, the body, every URL (including inside HTML attachments), and a SHA-256 of each attachment.
3. An MCP server checks SPF / DKIM / DMARC and the Received chain, then fans out every URL, attachment hash, and relay IP to reputation lookups (URLhaus, ThreatFox, urlscan).
4. Results are merged, scored, and posted to Telegram as a MALICIOUS / SUSPICIOUS / BENIGN verdict.

### Setup
- Deploy the bundled MCP server (Node.js) and note its URL.
- Import the workflow and add Google Sheets, Google Drive, and Telegram credentials.
- Point the four MCP Client nodes at your server URL and pick the matching tool.
- Set the sheet column and your Telegram chat ID, then run a test with the sample email.

## 1. Intake & Parse
Google Sheets Trigger pulls a flagged email; Download file fetches it from Drive. Code (JS) rejects non-`.eml`/`.msg`; Code (Python) extracts headers, URLs, and attachment hashes.

## 2. Header check
MCP Client runs check_email_headers: SPF / DKIM / DMARC and the Received chain. Returns an auth verdict and the relay IPs to investigate.

## 3. IOC investigation
Split IOCs fans each URL / hash / IP into its own item; Switch routes by type. Three MCP Clients check reputation: check_url, file_hash, lookup_ip.

## 4. Reporting
Merge gathers all results; Build Report scores them and writes the verdict; Notify Telegram sends the report to your chat.

## Before you run
Set the MCP server URL on all four MCP Client nodes and your Telegram chat ID on Notify Telegram — the workflow errors without them.

description: Automatically investigate a suspected phishing email and post a verdict (MALICIOUS / SUSPICIOUS / BENIGN) to Telegram. Parses the email, checks SPF/DKIM/DMARC and the Received chain, scans every URL and attachment hash, and looks up relay IPs against threat-intel feeds via a local MCP server.
